Situation1: There is a scheduled family gathering on the calendar.
Situation2: The meeting will cover key project updates that won’t be summarized elsewhere.
Story: I stared at my calendar, heart pounding. The family gathering had been planned for weeks—my daughter and her kids were so excited, and I’d promised to bake cookies with my granddaughter. She’d even called last night to remind me, her little voice bubbling with anticipation. But then, an email popped up from work: an urgent team meeting, scheduled at the exact same time. The project was at a critical stage, and my manager made it clear that everyone’s input was needed. There would be no summary, no recording—miss it, and I’d be out of the loop. I could already imagine my colleagues’ disappointment if I didn’t show up, and the subtle shift in their trust. Yet, the thought of letting down my family, especially my granddaughter, made my chest tighten. I felt pulled in two directions, each demanding my presence, each expecting me to put them first. I sat at my desk, torn, the weight of both worlds pressing down on me as I tried to figure out what to do.
